title: sprites.dat

spec.name: Image
spec.description: The images.dat entry of the sprite's main image, created with the sprite. Its animation script may add further images.

spec.name: Health Bar
spec.description: Width of the health bar in pixels. The bar is drawn in 3-pixel boxes, so the width is rounded down to 3n + 1, and it is at least 19. Its height comes from the unit (taller with shields and energy). 0 is used for sprites without a bar.

spec.name: Unused
spec.description: Not used: no code in StarCraft or StarEdit reads this field, in any version from 1.04 to 1.17. In the shipped file it is 1 for the sprites of units, their remains and buildings, and 0 for the rest.

spec.name: Visible
spec.description: 0 makes the sprite start hidden and seen by no player, until other code shows it. Only the Scanner Sweep's sprite, circle14 and the Subterranean Spines hit sprite have 0.

spec.name: Selection Circle
spec.description: Size of the selection circle: images.dat entry 561 + the value is the circle around your own units (22, 32, 48, 62, 72, 94, 110, 122, 146 and 224 pixels wide for 0 to 9), and 571 + the value the dashed circle around other players' units. The health bar is placed using the height of the circle image.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and 9 (higher values pick whatever images follow).

spec.name: Selection Circle Offset
spec.description: How far below the sprite's position the selection circle is drawn, in pixels. It is a signed byte, so 128 to 255 move the circle up (255 is one pixel up). The health bar goes 8 pixels below the circle.
spec.values: Integer value between −128 and 127, stored as a byte.

appendices.name: Appendix: Sprites list
appendices.description: Every sprite, with the units that use it (through flingy.dat), its image and that image's GRP file (from arr\images.tbl). Sprites 0 to 129 are tileset doodads. All taken from the shipped data files.

description:
sprites.dat holds the data of every sprite. A sprite is the object on the map that carries the images of a unit, a bullet or a doodad. Each entry gives the sprite's first image and whether it starts visible. For the sprites of units, it also gives the size of the health bar and the selection circle.

The file is arr\sprites.dat in the game's MPQ archives. It has 517 sprites and is 3229 bytes long. It is stored field by field, not entry by entry: first the Image of every sprite, then the Health Bar values, and so on, with nothing in between. The offsets below count from the start of the file.

Three fields are shorter than the others: Health Bar, Selection Circle and Selection Circle Offset. Sprites 0 to 129 are doodads that are part of the tileset, which never have a health bar or a selection circle, so these fields only have entries for sprites 130 to 516 (387 entries). The game reads them at the sprite number minus 130. If a unit were given a doodad sprite, the game would read the memory in front of the field.

The layout is the same in every version from 1.04 to 1.17, in both StarCraft and Brood War. StarCraft 1.00 to 1.03 used an older layout with 386 entries (2081 bytes). That older file is still in StarDat.mpq in later versions, but it is never loaded, because the game finds the copy in BrooDat.mpq (or patch_rt.mpq) first.

The game loads the file each time a game starts. StarEdit reads it as well (all fields except Health Bar). If the file is longer than the layout, the game stops with a file error. A shorter file loads without an error if it ends exactly where a field ends; the missing fields then keep whatever they held before. Out-of-range values are not rejected: the game then reads whatever follows the table that the value points into.
